title: 2022 AMC 12B Problem 4
statement: For how many values of the constant \(k\) will the polynomial \(x^2 + kx + 36\) have two distinct integer roots?

solutions.text:
If the roots are integers \(p\) and \(q,\) then \(pq = 36\) and \(k = -(p+q).\) Distinct roots must have the same sign, so we list factor pairs of \(36\) with \(p \ne q.\)

The positive pairs are \((1,36), (2,18), (3,12), (4,9),\) and the negative pairs are \((-1,-36),\) \((-2,-18),\) \((-3,-12),\) \((-4,-9).\) The pair \((6,6)\) is excluded since the roots must be distinct.

Each of these \(8\) pairs gives a different value of \(k.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
